## Personality

Quiet, steady and soft-spoken, he lets his wife do the talking and seems happy about it. He knows every rock in the bay.

## Lore

Cobb is forty-four, a fisherman of the bay, and the quietest member of the loudest family in the Fish Market. He is married to Gwennol, whose voice carries across the whole market, and he is perfectly happy to let her do the talking. He is the son of Wenna the net-mender and the father of Lowen and Bree. He is steady and soft-spoken, and he knows every rock in the bay.

### The little boat

Cobb fishes from a small open boat called the Puffin, which his grandfather built more than sixty years ago from timber he hauled down from the hills himself. She has been patched, re-planked and re-caulked so many times that there may not be a single original board left in her, but Cobb says she is still his grandfather's boat, and nobody argues with him. He takes her out before dawn every day the weather allows and is back by mid-morning, so that Gwennol has fish to sell while it is still fresh.

His father, Davey, fished the bay from the same boat until he died of a winter fever twelve years ago. Cobb learned the water from him the old way: by rowing it, by watching it, and by losing nets to every rock until he remembered where they were. He can tell you the depth over any rock in the bay from the colour of the water above it, and he has never lost a net to one since he was twenty.

### Torn nets

Twice this year Cobb's nets have come up torn clean through. Not snagged or frayed, as a rock or a dogfish might leave them, but opened in a long straight rent, as if something had simply gone through them. Both times it was in the deeper water just inside the headland, where he has fished all his life. His mother mended both nets on the fish market steps and announced to the whole market that no fish she ever knew made tears like that. Cobb did not disagree.

He has said nothing about it to the council, because he is not the kind of man who speaks at councils, but he has stopped going out past the middle of the bay. He always meant to take his son out deeper with him, once Lowen was old enough. Now he wants to know what tore his nets before he takes anyone out there.

### His son

Lowen did not wait. He signed on as a deckhand aboard Captain Corwin's Heron for a trading voyage along the coast, against his father's wishes. Cobb has not shouted about it; Gwennol did enough shouting for both of them. He knows the Heron is the most careful ship in the harbour and that Corwin has not lost a crate in twenty years. He also knows that crates are not sons. He is proud of the boy and frightened for him, and he has not yet found the words for either.

His daughter Bree is the opposite of him in every way, and he adores her. She tells him everything, at length, and he listens to every word.

### What he wants and fears

Cobb wants a quiet bay and his family around the table in the evening. He fears whatever is out past the middle of the bay, and he fears it more because he cannot name it.

### Hooks

A quest could go out with Cobb in the Puffin to see what tears his nets, or bring him proof of what it was so that he can finally sleep.
